stories.headline: Johnson and Glenn match wits once again as the Bears host the Jets in Week 4
stories.summary: — Ben Johnson's time in Detroit — a formative experience that led to his current job as coach of the Chicago Bears — was shaped in part by going against Aaron Glenn's defense in practice with the Lions.
stories.body:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- — Ben Johnson's time in Detroit — a formative experience that led to his current job as coach of the Chicago Bears — was shaped in part by going against Aaron Glenn's defense in practice with the Lions.


Johnson remembers it well.


“He certainly lights a fire under you," he said. “I still remember to this day being next to him in training camp, and you can hear him. You can hear him. And when the defense makes a play, he lets you know."


Johnson goes up against Glenn once again on Sunday when the Bears host the New York Jets. Glenn took over in New York in January 2025, right after Johnson was hired by Chicago.


Johnson, 40, was the offensive coordinator for Detroit while Glenn, 54, was the defensive coordinator with the Lions. Glenn faced their former boss last weekend, losing to 31-24 to Dan Campbell's Lions in Detroit.


Glenn recalled planning for practice with Johnson in one of their first meetings after he took over the offense.


“Just having those conversations and seeing how he put things together, and then just talking offensive and defensive football was good to have,” Glenn said. "But the one thing, we were so competitive in move-the-ball situations on how we wanted to beat each other, but it made both of us better, I will say that. He’s a damn good coach.”


Glenn and New York are preparing for a Chicago team with an uncertain situation at quarterback, at least publicly. Caleb Williams is rehabbing a right hamstring injury. Case Keenum passed for two touchdowns in Monday night's win over Philadelphia, but Johnson hasn't identified the starter for the matchup with the Jets.


Chicago also could go with Tyson Bagent, who emerged from the NFL’s concussion protocol on Sunday.


Whoever gets the call for the Bears will face an improved Jets defense, directed by Glenn, who was a defensive back in the NFL for 15 seasons.


“You can see how he played the game as a player has translated to how he coaches, and his guys take that same identity as well,” Johnson said. "Like I said, a ton of respect for him and he’s a heck of a competitor.”


Need to know
New York Jets (1-2) at Chicago (2-1).


When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, Fox.


Latest odds: Bears by 3 1/2.


Against the spread: Jets 2-1, Bears 2-1.


Last week: Jets lost to the Lions 31-24; Bears beat the Eagles 27-7.


Last meeting: Jets beat the Bears 31-10 on Nov. 27, 2022.


Series record: Bears lead 9-4.


Matchup to watch
Jets WR Garrett Wilson vs. Bears CB Jaylon Johnson. Wilson is coming off his best game of the season, catching 10 passes for 107 yards and a touchdown in last weekend's loss at Detroit. Wilson was a rookie the previous time the teams played, and he scored on receptions of 8 and 54 yards in a runaway victory for the Jets in 2022. Johnson has played a role in an impressive turnaround for Chicago's defense after a rough Week 1 at Carolina.


Stats and stuff
— The Jets enter with the NFL’s second-ranked defense, allowing 258.3 yards per game.


— New York has not had an interception in an NFL-record 20 consecutive games. The Jets’ most recent INT came in the 2024 season finale, when Ashtyn Davis had two against Miami.


— Geno Smith leads the NFL with a 75.5% completion rate, the highest by a Jets quarterback through Week 3 in franchise history with a minimum of three starts. He has passed for 783 yards and four TDs with no interceptions.


— Third-year RB Braelon Allen will likely serve as the primary ballcarrier out of the backfield with Breece Hall expected to be sidelined with a quadriceps injury.


— Chicago allowed a total of 16 points in the second half of its first three games.


— D'Andre Swift has 253 yards rushing for Chicago, and Kyle Monangai has 178. They could become the first duo to each rush for more than 200 yards for the Bears in the first four weeks of a season since Walter Payton and Roland Harper in 1978.


— Bears safety Dillon Thieneman leads the team with 21 total tackles. He is the only rookie in the NFL with at least 20 tackles, an INT and at least three passes defensed.


------


AP Pro Football Writer Dennis Waszak Jr. contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey schedule hacks: Add more Bruins and Hurricanes to your team
stories.summary: The NHL schedule isn't equal, so use that to your advantage when setting your fantasy hockey lineups in October.
stories.body:
It's never too early to hack the schedule in your fantasy favor, knowing the most effective way to seize an edge on your competition is to maximize every player's opportunity to contribute. By figuring out which teams are more active when most others are not, you seize greater flexibility in boosting your lineup's potential each night. The larger number of players in action on every occasion provides the greater capacity for positive fantasy returns. This advantage hits even harder in tight head-to-head competition, where each point can mean the difference between weekly victory and defeat.

Setting the benchmark at six games, as usual -- when another 20 teams, at minimum, are idle -- a handful of teams are worth recognizing when deciding which available players to keep or stream, all else being equal, on so-called slower nights from Oct. 1 to Oct. 31. The Boston Bruins and Buffalo Sabres lead the way in competing on seven such occasions when most of the rest of the league is off, while a trio of others -- also mentioned below -- do so on six dates. The ability to roll out the following fantasy figures when few others are active, then bench them when off on busier slates, could prove a winning formula in competition where lineups are set every day.

More: Sign up for free | Rankings | Projections | League types

Boston Bruins

One of only two teams to compete on seven lighter dates in October, the Bruins are ripe with streamable options, with winger JJ Peterka leading the way. Rostered in only 41.9% of ESPN Fantasy leagues, the Boston newbie is pegged to skate on a top line and power play with David Pastrnak and Elias Lindholm. One game in, the 24-year-old already has a (very pretty) goal on his 2026-27 resume. After an inferior showing in Utah last year, Peterka is undoubtedly feeling extra motivated to prove himself. Again, keeping on-ice company with Pastrnak also figures largely here.

On the blue line, Hampus Lindholm merits a look in deeper leagues, particularly through the first half of October. When healthy, as he is right now, the veteran defender has a history of riding a 0.41 point/game pace, while firing on net and blocking shots often enough. He's also subbing in on the Bruins' top power play, while Charlie McAvoy rides out his six-game suspension. A worthy streamer in the here and now, Lindholm is overwhelmingly available in ESPN Fantasy competition.

Slotted next to Fraser Minten on the third line and secondary power play, rookie James Hagens could be worth a flier in exceptionally large re-draft leagues. The rookie is at least worth observing while he gets his NHL feet wet, rather than damp. Hagens logged one assist through two regular season games in 2025-26.

Buffalo Sabres

It's fascinating how little fantasy interest the Sabres are garnering altogether, considering how many of their younger players are projected to take a productive leap forward this campaign. For instance, Josh Doan and Zach Benson should both eclipse the 60-point plateau, with goals taking up a good percentage of those points. Ahead of puck-drop, the pair of young men appear slotted in on Buffalo's top power play with Tage Thompson and Rasmus Dahlin.

Looking at the slightly older crowd, the biggest knock on Josh Norris is his inability to remain healthy. While there's no ignoring the forward's too colorful injury history, he's feeling fairly fit right now. If that good fortune lasts through the campaign's first three weeks -- and goodness gracious, hopefully much longer -- he certainly deserves a hard look in all but the shallowest of fantasy leagues. Norris is good for near a point/game when active.

Like the Bruins, Lindy Ruff's crew competes on seven so-called short nights through the first full month of the season.

ESPN Fantasy Hockey is the fun, free way to get inside the game. Draft your players, set your lineups and earn points when the pros do. Sign up today!

Anaheim Ducks

Not only do they play on six occasions when most of the league is off, but five of those tilts are at home, where the Ducks strung together a 24-13-4 record this past season. Beyond Cutter Gauthier, Leo Carlsson and Beckett Sennecke - who are all likely spoken for in the majority of ESPN leagues -- Mikael Granlund merits consideration as a streamer or injury substitute to launch 2026-27. The freshly-minted captain is competing on Anaheim's top power play along with the secondary scoring line. Available in nearly 40% of ESPN leagues, he'll put up a reasonable number of points.

Otherwise, keep an eye on A.J. Greer. Coach Joel Quenneville recently offered the former Panther a practice turn on the Ducks' top line with Carlsson and Gauthier. An interesting idea, after Greer "erupted" (it's all relative) for 17 goals and 15 assists in 78 games this past season. It certainly doesn't hurt to stay on top of the situation, particularly in deeper fantasy leagues.

As for between the pipes, I'm wary to endorse Lukas Dostal with the Ducks' refurbished defense in place. Let's first place the talented goalie on the wait-and-see shelf and give the inexperienced blue line an opportunity to surprise.

Calgary Flames

While Calgary's roster isn't exactly crowded with high-end fantasy talent, it also isn't fully devoid. Since someone needs to score for the Flames, Matt Coronato projects as the early choice to lead that list of someones. Entering his third full NHL season, the top-line winger sports 30-goal/30-assist potential.

After putting up 20 points in 37 games his first season, Matvei Gridin -- Coronato's linemate on the top unit and No. 1 power play -- serves as a true fantasy wild card at age 20. The first-round draft selection (2024) made even more productive noise in his AHL run with the Wranglers. Also entering his first full campaign with the Flames, defender Zayne Parekh is forecast to lead the blue line in production, particularly with the extra skater. I realize we're focusing on potential here, but rebuilding or not, the Flames are still going to put points on the board.

No rush here though. Despite suiting up on six lighter dates total, Calgary's schedule doesn't really deserve hacking until the final week of the month, when the club faces the Toronto Leafs, Edmonton Oilers and Seattle Kraken on exceptionally light nights (they also play the Colorado Avalanche on a busier Saturday). Flag your favorite fantasy Flames in the meanwhile.

Made it this far? Create your own league with your own rules and play against your friends today.

Carolina Hurricanes

Check your wire to see if Jackson Blake, Logan Stankoven or Taylor Hall is available. Then consider picking up one of them, in that prioritized order, for the first two full weeks of October, at minimum. After battling the Washington Capitals and Philadelphia Flyers Oct. 2 and 3, the Hurricanes play the Montreal Canadiens, Vancouver Canucks, Chicago Blackhawks and Philly (again) the next week. A friendly enough schedule. Tilts with Washington, Winnipeg and Calgary follow that stretch, with the Flames' date falling on a Sunday featuring only one other NHL contest.

Considering how productive they were in the postseason (combing for 55 points in 19 games) I'm surprised at the lackluster fantasy interest in this trio. Blake is 23 years old, Stankoven is 22, and even Hall is proving he's still got plenty in the tank at 34. The playoff performance from this dynamite scoring line doesn't feel flukey in the slightest.

At the opposing end of the busy-night spectrum, the Maple Leafs, Vegas Golden Knights, Capitals and Winnipeg Jets play only once when most of the rest of the league is off.

stories.headline: UFC 332 preview and picks: Why haven't there been more women's fights?
stories.summary: Top storylines and coaches' analysis for UFC 332 in Salt Lake City.
stories.body:
For all of the growth and progress of women's MMA over the past 15 years, the 2026 schedule has raised an uncomfortable -- but glaring -- question: What is happening to women's fights? Saturday's UFC 332 event in Salt Lake City will mark the first UFC event this year headlined by women, when Natalia Silva (20-5-1) and Wang Cong (10-1) meet for the vacant flyweight title. This year's lack of high-profile women's fights (and the excitement that should accompany them) has been impossible to miss. Wang, the 34-year-old Chinese challenger, has certainly felt it in the buildup to Saturday.

"Everyone was talking about how bad this main event is," Wang told ESPN, through an interpreter. "Of course I know about it. I think me and my opponent will prove them wrong, and show this is a fight they need to watch."

The sport could definitely use a boost. According to ESPN Research, the UFC has promoted 415 total bouts this year; 56 have featured women. That 13% split is the lowest mark in a decade.

The last women's fight to headline any UFC event was a non-title bout between Mackenzie Dern and Amanda Ribas in January 2025. For the last women's fight to headline a numbered event, one has to go all the way back to a bantamweight title fight between Amanda Nunes and Irene Aldana in June 2023.

Those trends are unlikely to change if some of the more underlying metrics continue to hold. Women's fights are increasingly being pushed to the prelims portion of events. In 2026, 83% of women's fights have appeared on prelims, compared with 72% in 2024, 61% in 2021 and 54% in 2017.

For their part, both Wang and Silva, a 29-year-old challenger out of Brazil, are predicting a memorable matchup Saturday. Wang is a former professional kickboxer with an aggressive style. Silva is known as more of a matador, but in 2024 when she went against Jessica Andrade, the most aggressive opponent of her UFC career, they won fight of the night.

"For sure, it's going to be a well-fought battle," Silva told ESPN through an interpreter. "She comes in aggressive, which gives me the opportunity to be aggressive as well. What I can tell people is that's going to be an incredible fight."

One thing is undeniable, Wang and Silva have a rare opportunity on Saturday to headline a numbered event with a women's title fight.

More storylines to watch
Gautier is getting the step up in competition he asked for
Ateba Gautier is an athletic, 24-year-old wrecking ball from Cameroon with a 5-0 record in the UFC that includes four knockouts. The combined record of his opponents, however, has been 4-14. That doesn't diminish what Gautier has done, but it's still unknown how he will fare against tougher competition.

For his part, Gautier isn't shying away from challenging himself. Immediately following his last win in May, Gautier called for a fight with former middleweight champion Israel Adesanya -- arguably the greatest 185-pound fighter of all time. The UFC didn't give him Adesanya, but he did get Roman Kopylov, a 35-year-old Russian with 12 UFC bouts. A win wouldn't validate Gautier as a title contender, but it would prove he's ready for greater tests.

Wint could be the sleeper breakout candidate of the card
In terms of fighters who can make an individual splash at UFC 332, Wang and Silva in the main event stand out. Payton Talbott taking on a former champion in Deiveson Figueiredo is an obvious one. Undefeated Jacobe Smith is a finishing machine, and the aforementioned Gautier is in the biggest fight of his career.

Quietly, Anthony Wint could steal the show. Wint's prelim fight against Lucas Armand will be his third in less than two months. He's a former collegiate and NFL linebacker, fighting out of a notoriously talented and striking-oriented gym in Kill Cliff FC. He already is very much on UFC CEO Dana White's radar, having earned his contract on "Contender Series" on Aug. 11. If he does something spectacular, expect White to give it attention in his postfight comments (which in turn, draws everyone's attention).

Coaches' questions for women's flyweight championship
'What is Natalia Silva's game plan under pressure?'

Cong's striking is on point. She is aggressive with it, but she makes mistakes with it as well. I feel like Silva is the more well-rounded fighter, and it's up to her to take advantage of that. If this fight does go to the ground, I think Silva will present bigger problems -- and I see that as a path to victory for her. Wang is going to look for the knockout, and because of that, she will overextend in certain positions. I have a gut feeling Silva is going to work some ground work into this one. Silva is so good at controlling the pace of a fight, but with Cong coming at her so aggressively, I think she'll be forced to try different stuff. It's a pick 'em fight. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

Who will own the 'second exchange'?
Silva's path to victory is about space, timing and making Wang reset. Silva needs to use her movement and feints to keep Wang from getting comfortable and building combinations. Silva is best at range, not standing in the pocket. Her counters matter in this matchup. She doesn't just survive Wang's pressure, she scores with midrange kicks and southpaw counters after Wang overcommits. For Wang, it's about pressure without chasing. She needs to cut the cage. Containing Silva becomes the real job. This is where her low kick and body work become weapons. Silva's movement is a huge part of her defense. If Wang can consistently attack the legs and body, she can start shrinking the cage without simply chasing. Who controls what happens after the initial exchange? If Wang attacks, Silva counters and exits, that's Silva's fight. If Wang attacks, Silva tries to exit and Wang cuts her off, those are the moments Wang wants. Whoever imposes their will on that second exchange wins. -- Eric Nicksick, Xtreme Couture

stories.headline: UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case
stories.summary: UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.
stories.body:
MADRID -- UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.

Payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to José María Enriquez Negreira -- the former vice-president of Spain's Technical Committee of Referees -- over two decades have been subject to a UEFA investigation since 2023, while there is also an ongoing Spanish criminal case.

Barcelona have said the payments, which totaled over €7 million ($7.9m), were made for technical refereeing reports.

- Ronaldo's Portugal walkout is nothing new; he has a long history of rows with coaches

- Source: Mbappé to be available for Clásico

- Raphinha back at Barça, injured in Brazil game

"UEFA can confirm that it has received from Real Madrid CF a substantial amount of documents related to the ongoing investigation into FC Barcelona in the matter involving José María Enríquez Negreira," UEFA confirmed in a statement on Thursday.

"The UEFA Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors have also received these latest documents which they will assess as part of their ongoing review."

Real Madrid said the dossier included "extensive documentation and evidence regarding events of extraordinary seriousness, which directly affect the integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system."

"Real Madrid C.F. considers it essential that, now that UEFA has this documentation, the investigation proceeds with the utmost urgency until its full conclusion, and that the competent bodies take the appropriate decisions in accordance with the severity of the verified facts," the club said.

"Our club will continue to actively collaborate with UEFA and take all actions within its power to clarify events that it deems incompatible with the principles of integrity, transparency, and fair play that should govern European football."

In May, Madrid president Florentino Pérez said that the club was gathering evidence to submit a dossier to UEFA.

Having previously adopted a conciliatory tone with Barcelona -- saying in 2024 that the two clubs "have to help each other" as they worked together on the proposed European Super League -- Pérez has since been extremely critical of his LaLiga rivals.

"They've stolen seven league [titles] from me," Pérez said in May.

In a statement, Barcelona emphasized that Thursday's development did not equate to "any new proceedings."

"The proceedings were initiated in 2023, with the appointment of two investigators who have since carried out the action they deemed appropriate," Barcelona said. "The Club has always complied with all their requests. These proceedings have not been reopened because they have never been closed.

"The UEFA statement confirms receipt of documentation submitted by Real Madrid and indicates that the investigators will assess it within the framework of the existing investigation. The same text expressly refers, on two occasions, to an investigation and a review that are 'ongoing.' It therefore does not announce the opening, reopening, or reactivation of any proceedings, nor does it contain any assessment of the substance or value of the documentation provided.

"It is up to the investigators to determine what action, if any, they consider appropriate regarding this documentation. As of today, they have not made any new requests to FC Barcelona nor have they forwarded Real Madrid's complaint to the Club. Should they do so, the Club will respond accordingly, as it has done up to now.

"In accordance with the applicable legislation governing this matter, these proceedings are subject to the outcome of the criminal case currently being heard in Spain and will continue to be so."

stories.headline: Downing Street clarifies Andy Burnham's remarks on Man City case
stories.summary: A spokesperson for Andy Burnham has insisted the guilty verdict against Manchester City is "serious" after remarks the Prime Minister made about the case on Wednesday raised eyebrows.
stories.body:
A spokesperson for Andy Burnham has insisted the guilty verdict against Manchester City is "serious" after remarks the Prime Minister made about the case on Wednesday raised eyebrows.

Burnham told the BBC on Wednesday he would be "really concerned" if City's Abu Dhabi owners sold the club in the wake of City being found to have breached the Premier League's financial rules by an independent commission, crediting them with being "a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester."

Burnham also appeared to draw parallels between City's guilty verdict and the handling of a disciplinary case against Everton, the club he supports.

He said he still held the view very firmly that the Toffees were "not fairly treated" and added: "I remember people proclaiming Everton guilty at the time and with hindsight I think more people would say that wasn't fair, the way that was handled.

"So it would be wrong of me to leap to one side given the experience that I'd had before becoming Prime Minister."

Burnham's comments have drawn criticism on social media and shadow sports minister Louie French called for the Government to "keep politics out of football," with the case set to proceed to an appeal board and a sanctions hearing.

A No. 10 Downing Street spokesman said on Thursday: "As the Prime Minister made clear, the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules.

"He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected.

"If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences."

- Klopp not preparing for more titles after verdict against Man City

- Man City owners must sell due to 'shame of their guilt' - Jamie Carragher

Meanwhile, a parliamentary select committee wants answers from the permanent secretary of Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs (HMRC) regarding any tax implications of the City case.

The chair of the Treasury Committee, Dame Meg Hillier, has written to JP Marks asking whether he is aware of the commission's findings, in particular what it said about the use of "sham" arrangements to conceal liabilities to staff.

Hillier also asked Marks whether he had asked for an unredacted copy of the decision published on Tuesday.

"While I acknowledge that taxpayer confidentiality may inhibit what you can disclose, I would welcome reassurance from HMRC that you are seized of the importance of these issues and the public interest in the case," Hillier wrote.

City are expected to lodge an appeal against the guilty verdict before Friday's deadline, having claimed the commission's decision contained "clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe".

stories.headline: Jamal Shead, Raptors reach 3-year, $24M extension through 2029-30
stories.summary: Raptors guard Jamal Shead has agreed to a three-year, $24 million contract extension with the franchise, his agent, KJ Smith, told ESPN.
stories.body:
Toronto Raptors guard Jamal Shead has agreed to a three-year, $24 million contract extension with the franchise, his agent, KJ Smith, told ESPN on Thursday.

The new deal keeps Shead, 24, under contract through the 2029-30 season. He lands an extension just two seasons after the Houston product was selected with the 45th overall pick in the 2024 NBA draft.

The 6-foot-1 guard had 354 assists (5.4 per game) in 2025-26 -- a league-best off the bench and the most in franchise history for a reserve player. He played in all 82 regular-season games -- one of 18 NBA players to do so -- while averaging 6.6 points and 1.7 rebounds.

Shead saw action in seven playoff games (four starts), averaging nine points, five assists and 1.4 steals.

He ranked fifth in the league in assist-to-turnover ratio last season.

stories.headline: Lando Norris urges F1 and social media giants to help tackle abuse after Franco Colapinto ban feud
stories.summary: Lando Norris called on Formula 1 and social media companies to do more to combat online abuse after the torrent of messages he received following last weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Lando Norris called on Formula 1 and social media companies to do more to combat online abuse after the torrent of messages he received following last weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The comment sections of Norris' social media channels were filled with thousands of negative and hateful messages after he said in a postrace interview that Alpine driver Franco Colapinto should be banned for causing the collision that took his McLaren out of the race.

Two days after the event in Baku, Norris publicly apologized for his postrace comments in a message shared with his 11.9 million followers on Instagram.

Speaking ahead of this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Norris explained why he made the apology and called on the sport, social media channels and drivers to do more to prevent extreme comments, including death threats.

"I said what I wanted to Franco, and he's the only one really that I need to share my opinion with and share my apology with," Norris said. "I don't need to do it on social media, and I don't feel like I need to use social media to do such a thing, but at the same time, there obviously was a lot of that noise and stuff in the background, and I thought it was only sensible to announce or show that I made that apology.

"But yeah, at the same time, I do still see social media at times, and I saw some bits, some not so good, some better, but sadly that's what we deal with. I think a lot of sports deal with [it], some of it's down to just passion, and that's what you always have in sports.

"I think you see a lot more of it because social media is such an easy thing to share your opinions on. And to a certain extent, I completely respect it, but obviously to the extent of online abuse, death threats, all those things, those are things that I think are way too far beyond being a fan of a sport, or a driver, or a person, or an athlete, whatever it is.

"There's a line, but it's not new, it's something that's been around every sport for a long time, and I think just highlights more the fact that social media platforms, sports, need to do more, and maybe the people, the drivers, athletes, whoever, more to stop this kind of stuff from happening, because some people can deal with it much better than others."

Norris said the reaction he received on social media would not stop him from speaking his mind, even though he regretted his postrace comments in Baku.

"I should never have said the sort of stuff that I said, so I get why some people might have been more unhappy, let's just say upset, which is understandable," he added.

"Obviously there's that line which was crossed at times, quite a lot, which is not just being upset at someone, this is much, much worse.

"But I think I'm always happy, in general, in speaking my mind, and saying if I like things, don't like things, if I agree with things or not. I know I'm not able to please everyone, and you're never going to have everyone on your side, so I think that's normal enough, that's life, and that's what you have to come around to accept at the end of the day."

- Lewis Hamilton hits out at Ferrari hierarchy in Fred Vasseur defence: 'Point fingers somewhere else'

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: Where were today's drivers when F1 last raced at Sepang?

- Max Verstappen steps in for GT race at Portimão amid two F1 triple-headers

Colapinto accepted Norris' apology earlier this week, but on Thursday said he was surprised the McLaren driver chose to be so public with his criticism after the race.

"I think he was in the heat of the moment ... He knows what comments create because he suffered from it," Colapinto said.

"He was probably the driver that was speaking the most about hate a couple of years ago, just a few seasons ago. So I was very surprised. But then, of course, he apologised.

"Unfortunately, he also got a lot of hate from it. But I also felt it's a tricky situation with the outside world. And that's why I think we need to be a bit safe inside about the things we say. And I understand it in the heat of the moment to say things like that."

Colapinto's fanbase has proved particularly vocal online and as recently as the Spanish Grand Prix last month turned on his Alpine teammate Pierre Gasly, with abuse that included messages sent to the Frenchman's family and girlfriend.

Asked what his message to those posting the negative comments online would be, Colapinto said: "My message is always the same, that they sometimes don't realise what you can create by writing in your keyword, and that we are humans, and it's not easy for us when we get these kind of things.

"I think it always goes to Argentinians, but we miss that it doesn't come only from Argentinians. It comes a lot from them, I fully agree. It doesn't just come from them, and they are extremely passionate, and they support me a lot. And it's bad, and they are bad many times, but it comes from all the world, and from many other fanbases.

"I don't know if we are not seeing it, I get loads of it and no one ever talks about it. I mean, it's fine because I don't look at social media too much. I don't go into it. But I know it affects a lot of people, and a lot of drivers, and a lot of families more than me.

"I hope that they improve. I've been asking for a long time. It's tricky for us drivers to control it. I think we are the ones to not do them more. But we are also really striving to improve the situation by ourselves. Because we try -- for me, it's been since last year that I've been talking about it. I am doing my best, but it's tricky."

In 2023 F1's governing body, the FIA, set up the United Against Online Abuse (UAOA) commission, which as recently as this year's British Grand Prix received the collective support of all 22 drivers in F1.

On its website, the UAOA says it "aims to design, develop and implement practical actions that can protect the integrity of sports across the world as safe and inclusive spaces for competitors, officials, journalists, and fans alike."

stories.headline: Banned and crowned: Isaac Heeney wins Swans' best and fairest
stories.summary: Isaac Heeney has been named Sydney's best and fairest, but he and fellow Sydney stars were notable absentees from the club's end-of-season awards night.
stories.body:
An absent Isaac Heeney has been crowned Sydney's best and fairest as the spectre of sexual assault allegations continues to loom over the AFL club.

Heeney was not at Sydney Town Hall to accept his third consecutive Bob Skilton medal, having requested to skip the club's Thursday awards night.

Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, James Jordon and Riley Bice were also absent after serving a club-imposed suspension with Heeney throughout the finals.

Despite missing Round 24 and two finals -- which also counted for award calculations -- Heeney polled 431 votes to comfortably claim the club's highest individual annual honour ahead of ruck Brodie Grundy (400) and key forward Charlie Curnow (398).

Four of the suspended Swans finished in the top 10 of the count, with Warner placing fourth ahead of Blakey (seventh) and Jordon (10th).

The club had opted against changing eligibility and voting criteria for the Bob Skilton medal, following suit after the AFL did the same with the Brownlow Medal.

The league did not invite Heeney or Warner to last week's Brownlow ceremony.

In his awards ceremony speech, Swans chairman Andrew Pridham said the reasoning behind the club's eligibility criteria was two-fold - protecting the integrity of votes; and ensuring off-field matters were separate from on-field performance.

"We do not believe it would have been appropriate to retrospectively remove votes that have already been cast owing to the subsequent incident," Pridham said.

"The medals awarded tonight acknowledge on-field performance across the season.

"Erasing a season of football after the fact would, in our opinion, be inappropriate and in excess of a sanction.

"I can assure you that we did not make any decisions we have made in recent times like that.

"I respect that some people in this room and beyond may not agree with where we have landed tonight.

"It has been very, very difficult, but let me be equally clear that these decisions to allow the players to remain eligible does not diminish our concern and respect for everyone involved in this."

Independent of the AFL-endorsed club bans for what the Swans termed a "serious breach of expected club behaviour and standards", a police investigation into an alleged sexual assault at the Pullman Hotel is ongoing.

Detectives in early September travelled to NSW to interview a 30-year-old Maroubra man, a 25-year-old Paddington man and two Randwick men aged 25 and 26.

It is understood the men interviewed were Heeney, Warner, Jordon and Blakey.

No charges have been laid. AAP is not suggesting any wrongdoing on the part of the suspended players.

The five banned players have since returned to Swans headquarters after serving their suspension and individually offered apologies to colleagues and teammates following their team's preliminary final loss to Fremantle.

Heeney was the only player after the club meeting to address media and did so with a brief statement.

"It was really nice to address the whole club," the 30-year-old said on September 23.

"Extremely thankful they could give us their time and understanding, so yeah, it was really good."

Victoria Police's eight-week timeline prediction - which was first flagged on September 2 - on their investigation into the Pullman Hotel incident takes in the free agency and trade period (October 2-14).

All five players are contracted for next year, with Blakey signed to the club until 2031.

Warner and Jordon come off contract at the end of 2027, while Heeney and Bice are signed until the end of 2028.

Multiple reports have suggested Blakey is seeking a trade to a Victorian club, but Sydney football boss Leon Cameron dismissed those rumblings as "speculation" in September.

stories.headline: St. Louis up to 2nd place with unbeaten run now at 17 games
stories.summary: Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.

St. Louis (13-6-8) extended its unbeaten streak to 17 matches in MLS play and moved up to second place in MLS' Western Conference table.

New York (9-12-6) entered having conceded just two goals in its last four games, with Ethan Horvath recording three shutouts.

The Red Bulls had won their last two games, but were without rising stars Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall for the game, with the pair away on national team duty for the United States.

Rafael Navarro opened the scoring just five minutes into the game when he redirected Conrad Wallem's header across the goal.

Becher capitalized on a New York turnover deep in its own half to make it 2-0 in the 87th minute. Ostrak sent in a rebound in stoppage time.

Roman Bürki made four saves to earn his third clean sheet of the season for St. Louis.

It was the first time New York and St. Louis have met during the regular season.

St. Louis hosts the LA Galaxy next on Oct. 11, while the Red Bulls play San Diego FC at home the day before.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Ivan: Nathan Cleary can get even better after Dally M
stories.summary: Ivan Cleary has spoken of the horror of watching his son Nathan's leg injury, and a belief he can still get better again after winning his first Dally M.
stories.body:
Ivan Cleary has admitted watching his son Nathan suffer a badly broken leg marked one of the hardest days of his career, feeling the line between father and coach blurred for the first time.

But the veteran Penrith mentor is insistent his son Nathan still has more levels to attain once he returns from his injury, following his landmark Dally M victory on Wednesday night.

Cleary's Dally M triumph completed the Penrith halfback's rugby league box set, having now claimed every major team and individual honour available to him by age 28.

Unable to attend in person after being released from hospital following emergency surgery on his leg, the Panthers halfback collected the game's top honour while in a wheelchair at home.

Coach Ivan also appeared emotional during Nathan's pre-recorded speech, after the trophy was hand-delivered to the halfback earlier in the day.

"His voice perked up from what it's been the past couple of days," Ivan told AAP.

"It's a pretty amazing award. You don't play the game for individual awards, but it's certainly nice to be recognised.

"Particularly this award, it's pretty much the No.1 award in the game."

Reminded that his son had now scaled virtually every possible mountain in the sport, the Penrith coach insisted there were still improvements left in his son's game.

"It's crazy," Ivan said.

"I know he'd say it and I probably think a bit the same. You don't reflect too much when it's still going on. But when you put it like that, it's amazing.

"But I know there is so much more to come as well, and I know he thinks that way as well."

Nathan has received positive early news from surgeons after the operation on his compound fracture and dislocated ankle, as a result of a hip-drop tackle in Sunday's preliminary-final loss to Newcastle.

He will soon undergo surgery on other foot after fighting through a broken bone to play the Knights, but Penrith are hopeful he will be right for round one in 2027.

"Sunday was definitely one of the harder days I have been through," coach Cleary said.

"It's the first time where the line of dad and coach got a bit blurred. And the loss, I guess we have had a lot of good days so you can't have it all your way.

"Very emotional, but life goes on."

Footage has also emerged of fullback Dylan Edwards not only being horrified by the graphic injury at first, but then also trying to stop Nathan from seeing it.

"I was just trying to keep him calm as I could," Edwards said.

"To his credit he is a tough person. And the way he was handling that was incredible.

"It was gut-wrenching, something you're not used to seeing on the footy field."

Edwards, meanwhile, is still hopeful of being able to represent Australia at the World Cup after avoiding knee surgery following a PCL injury in the loss.

"I'm not sure, I have to talk to Kevvie (coach Kevin Walters)," Edwards said, while wearing a brace at the Dally Ms.

stories.headline: WNBA playoffs 2026: Caitlin Clark, A'ja Wilson and keys to Fever-Aces Game 3
stories.summary: Las Vegas hosts Indiana on Thursday with the winner advancing to the WNBA semifinals. Here's what could decide the game.
stories.body:
LAS VEGAS -- The No. 3 seed Las Vegas Aces are the WNBA's defending champions and out to prove they are still the league's boss. The No. 6 seed Indiana Fever know they're about to be as popular in Vegas as the house constantly winning.

After the Fever's 99-89 win over the Aces on Tuesday in Indianapolis evened their first-round series 1-1, the teams meet Thursday (9 p.m. ET) to decide who moves on to the semifinals. The Aces have won three of the past four championships. The Fever's lone title came in 2012.

Emotions will run high at Michelob Ultra Arena for Game 3. On Tuesday, Aces star A'ja Wilson objected to a fan pointing at her from behind the basket and left the court to confront him.

The WNBA rulebook bars players or coaches from going into the stands to confront spectators. But on Thursday, the league announced there would be no further discipline for Wilson or any other Aces involved in the incident.

Aces fans will be fired up to support their team. The Fever haven't had much luck in Las Vegas until this season. The Aces moved to the city in 2018, and Indiana did not win a game there until July 5, an 84-68 victory. Then the Fever won again, this time 109-75, in Las Vegas a week later.

Indiana almost made it a regular-season sweep on Aug. 6 in Indianapolis but blew a 20-point lead and then fell 86-84 in overtime. Back in Las Vegas for the teams' playoff opener Sunday, the Aces dominated 102-85.

Now the teams meet for the sixth and final time in 2026. Here's what might decide which team moves on. And be sure to come back when the game tips for live analysis, updates and highlights.

Can the Fever replicate Tuesday's defense?

During the regular season, the Fever ranked ninth in defensive rating (estimate of points allowed per 100 possessions) at 110.3, and the Aces were fifth (107.2). Las Vegas was better on both ends of the court in Game 1, and Indiana knew it had to improve its defense Tuesday to keep its season going.

The Fever did that, at times frustrating all the Aces except Jackie Young, whom they could not stop (31 points). The Aces still scored 89 points. But during both the second and third quarters, the Fever held the Aces to 17 points.

That put Indiana in the driver's seat for the fourth quarter. The Aces made a run, outscoring the Fever 29-27 in the final period, but the middle-game defense gave Indiana enough cushion.

"I thought we played with a back-against-the-wall desperation that you need to play with at playoff time," Indiana coach Stephanie White said.

Now they need to do that again.

How well will Wilson play?

It's rare to see Wilson lose her cool, but on Tuesday the Fever defense seemed to frustrate her at times. She was 5-of-11 from the field but 12-of-13 from the line. Wilson was the WNBA's leading scorer in the regular season and is one of the most clutch players in league history. That latter trait could make all the difference in Game 3.

Coach Becky Hammon thought defense was the Aces' biggest problem in Game 2. She said that kept them from being the offensive team they normally are, and that impacted Wilson's performance.

"I thought [the Fever] brought a lot of congestion [in the lane]," Hammon said. "Them picking up, being disruptive, got us out of our flow a little bit. At times, your offense has to help your defense. I thought defensively we were poor tonight, and the two are married together. We know when we're a good defensive team, we become very elite offensively."

Can the Fever guards do enough for a victory?

The backcourt of Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell has been one of the most entertaining shows in the WNBA all season, and it was outstanding Tuesday. Clark finished with 27 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds. Mitchell had 26 points.

The Fever also got strong defense from two other guards: starter Lexie Hull and reserve rookie Raven Johnson. Their energy was a big part of what helped the Fever rally and then take the lead after trailing 26-18 after the first quarter.

If the guards do their job, the Fever are formidable. But post player Aliyah Boston ultimately could be the difference-maker. She came back after a tough first quarter Tuesday and had 22 points. That was her highest scoring output since also getting 22 on Aug. 22.

Can Indiana slow down Jackie Young?

Young has 52 points and 15 assists through two games of this series. Like her teammates Wilson and Chelsea Gray, Young is a seasoned big-game player. That trio has won three WNBA championships together. And while Wilson is the perennial MVP candidate and Gray is the "Point Gawd," Young also has been indispensable for Las Vegas since being drafted No. 1 in 2019.

Wilson, Young and Gray are Hall of Fame-level players. But the Aces got nine points and five rebounds from starter Stephanie Talbot, too, and that's significant. Jewell Loyd and Cheyenne Parker-Tyus also can provide an offensive boost off the bench to back up the Aces' big three.

stories.headline: Texans host the Cowboys seeking their first win after an 0-3 start
stories.summary: — After a second straight 0-3 start to the season, any win would be huge for the Houston Texans.
stories.body:
HOUSTON -- — After a second straight 0-3 start to the season, any win would be huge for the Houston Texans.


But getting that elusive first win against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday would certainly mean a little something extra.


“We know how big this game is and how much it means to our fans here in the city of Houston,” coach DeMeco Ryans said. “We have to play well to give our fans what they’ve been searching for and that’s that first win and I’m excited.”


These teams don’t play very often, with Sunday being just the eighth all-time meeting, making these rare matchups a big deal in the state.


The Cowboys lead the series 4-3, but Houston has won two of the past three meetings, including a 34-10 victory in Arlington, Texas, in the most recent matchup in 2024. And diehard Texans fans still fondly remember when Houston got its first-ever win as a franchise with a 19-10 triumph over Dallas in 2002.


Now in their 25th season, Sunday’s game will be an anniversary celebration featuring a halftime ceremony honoring Texans greats including Hall of Famer Andre Johnson, J.J. Watt, Arian Foster, DeAndre Hopkins, Brian Cushing and Billy Miller along with former coach Gary Kubiak.


Houston defensive end Will Anderson is trying to stay focused this week despite all the hoopla surrounding the game.


“The biggest thing (is) how much more can we focus in on just doing your job and just being where you’re supposed to be and doing what you’re supposed to do,” he said. “Then when we get to the game, we can worry about the rivalry in Texas and stuff like that.”


While the Texans are one of five winless NFL teams this season, the Cowboys year hasn’t gone much better. Dallas is 1-2 after a 34-31 loss to Baltimore on a last-second field goal last week.


It’s a game that led to owner Jerry Jones saying he believes errors in game management by his coaching staff in the final seconds cost his team the win.


Dallas coach Brian Schottenheimer knows better than to underestimate the Texans despite another awful start.


“We know that we want to focus on us, but clearly when you watch them play, they’re not a 0-3 team,” he said. “Their record says they’re 0-3, but hard pressed to find a better defense than this front.”


Need to know
Dallas (1-2) at Houston (0-3)


When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, FOX


Latest odds: Texans by 3


Against the spread: Cowboys 2-1; Texans 0-3


Last week: Cowboys lost to the Ravens 34-31; Texans lost to the Colts 19-17.


Last meeting: Texans beat the Cowboys 34-10 on Nov. 18, 2024.


Series record: Cowboys lead 4-3.


Matchup to watch
The Cowboys have struggled under 34-year-old first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Dallas ranks 30th in the NFL by allowing 387 yards a game and is dealing with mounting injuries in the secondary.


The unit will be tested this week with the expected return of star receiver Nico Collins, who has missed the past two games with a hamstring injury. Quarterback C.J. Stroud ranks seventh in the NFL by averaging 264.7 yards passing a game but has thrown just three touchdown passes and will get a boost if Collins is back. Stroud hasn’t thrown an interception this season and hasn’t been picked off in six straight home games.


The Cowboys acquired cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Steelers on Thursday to help address their secondary issues. But he has been inactive in each game this season while upset about his contract situation and dealing with a back issue so it would seem unlikely that he’d play this week just days after arriving.


Stats and stuff
— The Texans went 12-2 after last year’s 0-3 start to become the first team in NFL history to reach the playoffs twice after losing the first three games. Only the 1992 Chargers rebounded from a 0-4 start to make the playoffs.


— Dallas QB Dak Prescott threw his 250th career TD pass last week to become the fifth player in NFL history with at least 250 touchdown passes and at least 30 rushing TDs.


— Houston DE Will Anderson had 2 ½ sacks, three tackles for loss, his fifth career forced fumble and fourth career fumble recovery last week. He’s second in the NFL with seven tackles for loss and his four sacks are tied for second in the league.


— Dallas WR CeeDee Lamb had seven receptions for 112 yards last week for his 29th career 100-yard game. Lamb ranks fourth in the NFL with 309 yards receiving this season and has had at least 110 yards receiving in the past two games.


— Houston DE Danielle Hunter forced the 16th fumble of his career last week. He has 21 ½ sacks and 25 tackles for loss in 19 home games since joining the Texans in 2024. He had two sacks and three tackles for loss in his previous game against Dallas.


------


AP Pro Football Writer Schuyler Dixon contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Why Matthew Stafford made a cameo in Taylor Swift's 'Patient Zero' music video
stories.summary: Why, yes, that was Matthew Stafford. Here's why all signs pointed to the reigning NFL MVP's music video cameo.
stories.body:
Never let it be said Matthew Stafford lacks range.

If you find yourself watching Taylor Swift's recently debuted music video for "Patient Zero" and see someone who happens to bear a striking resemblance to the Los Angeles Rams quarterback, that's because it is said quarterback.

In the video, which also stars actors Colin Farrell, Dakota Johnson and Cara Delevingne, the Super Bowl LVI champion and reigning NFL MVP makes a cameo at a black-tie affair alongside his wife, Kelly Stafford. Stafford's not the only athlete in the scene, as former Los Angeles Kings center and two-time Stanley Cup champion Jarret Stoll can be spotted next to him.

For those struck by the randomness of that duo appearing in a Swift video, you clearly don't know the lore.

So let's get into it.

The Staffords are friends with the 14-time Grammy Award winner and her husband, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, as are Stoll and his wife, Erin Andrews. The couples attended the Madison Square Garden wedding of Swift and Kelce this summer alongside Charissa Thompson and her significant other, Steven Cundari -- the latter of whom is also featured in the black-tie event scene of Swift's video posing next to Farrell.

As for Andrews and Thompson, the duo have been vocal supporters of Swift and the Kansas City Chiefs star's relationship since before they started dating, even making a plea on their "Calm Down" podcast for the singer to give Kelce a chance. Meanwhile, the Staffords' four daughters are known Swift fans, with Kelly sharing in 2024 that she and Matthew surprised the girls with a trip to see "The Eras Tour" in New Orleans. Kelly and her daughters also attended the June premiere of "Toy Story 5" in Los Angeles where Swift made a surprise appearance to perform her song "I Knew It, I Knew You."

Stafford said his daughters were one of the main reasons he agreed to appear in the video, which he filmed sometime during the offseason.

"They were right there with me," Stafford said. "That's one of the main reasons that I ended up going to do that. She wanted to offer an experience for our family and our kids to see that. I'm obviously really grateful and excited to be in it. My girls, as they do with all her songs, love that song. I was actually driving them to soccer yesterday and they were asking me to play it in the car so we had it on repeat. It's been good."

Stafford also came away impressed by getting an up-close look at Swift's creative process.

"It was cool. It was really cool," Stafford said. "It's cool for me, obviously for Kelly, for us two, but obviously for our kids too. Just to watch her do her thing is pretty impressive. From borderline directing, producing, writing, all of it, editing live as we were doing it. It was really cool to be a part of it. I've never been a part of it before. I probably won't ever be again based on my acting chops, but it was a cool day."

Then there's the Emmy's Easter egg of it all. Swift sent her fans into overdrive when she appeared via prerecorded video skit at the 87th Emmy Awards alongside her cat, Olivia Benson, and the show's host, Mariska Hargitay, who plays Swift's cat's namesake on "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit." In the sketch, the pop superstar addressed the camera and said, "I think what we're gonna be looking for is hiding in plain sight: Saccharide Aries from the vineyard north or south."

Upon the Stafford reveal, the "Aries" reference has been decoded as a nod to the symbol for the astrological sign for Aries being a ram. As for the rest of the cryptic message? "Saccharide" is a reference to Farrell's role in the show "Sugar," "from the vineyard" is the old French translation of Delevingne and "north or south" is a play on Dakota.

And while you ruminate on all of that, we're going to ponder how we got a Stafford Easter egg before the Tayvis wedding photos. Any day now.

ESPN NFL Nation reporter Sarah Barshop contributed to this story.

stories.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
stories.summary: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
stories.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)

The Manchester United midfielder was left out of Portugal's squad for Sunday's game against Norway.

"He played with an injury he brought from Manchester United," Portugal boss Jorge Jesus said. "He really wanted to play against Wales."

Patrick Dorgu (Manchester United)

The news for Manchester United fans who saw Fernandes absent worsened on Sunday when Dorgu was injured.

The left wing-back limped out of Denmark's match against Wales after 30 minutes.

Denmark head coach Brian Riemer told broadcaster TV2 after the game: "He has an injury and has to go home."

Cody Gakpo (Liverpool)

Liverpool forward Gakpo lasted only 17 minutes of the Netherlands' match against Serbia on Sunday. It means Liverpool are sweating over the fitness of Isak and Gakpo.

He looked in pain as he held the lower part of his right leg.

"It's his ankle, that's all I know," Netherlands boss Xavi Hernández said. "Tomorrow we will know, but hopefully it's not too important."

Noussair Mazraoui (Manchester United)

The United full-back was forced out of Morocco's Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Lesotho after 69 minutes. He was holding his back while on the floor after a challenge.

Nico O'Reilly (Manchester City)

O'Reilly missed England's win against Czechia on Tuesday night after also missing training on Monday. Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha was called into the matchday squad. O'Reilly returned to Manchester for further treatment before England played Croatia.

Jan Paul van Hecke (Tottenham Hotspur)

The Tottenham defender Jan Paul van Hecke picked up a foot injury in the Netherlands' clash with Serbia and withdrew from the Netherlands' squad during a training session.

No replacement will be called up for van Hecke. He is now returning to Spurs.

Embiid "full participant" in first Sixers' practice
Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday.

"He looked great," Nurse said of Embiid. "Very, very good news from the standpoint of where it's been the last couple years, last couple summers leading into today. ... It's great to see."

After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries.

He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain.

The only Sixers player who did not participate in Tuesday's practice according to a team spokesperson was backup big man Adem Bona, who is dealing with a sprained left foot.

Anfernee Simons, who signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract to join Philadelphia in July, said Embiid's presence in the gym was already notable leading up to the start of camp.

"Everybody's been impressed around here about how he's come in and worked," Simons said. "Joel is going to be Joel. He's going to be a dominant player always. We just want to continue for him to be himself, as well, and I think everybody's going to be able to work around that."

Despite the injuries, the 10-year veteran still averaged 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game last season.

Embiid's inclusion only added to what several Sixers players described as an "exciting" opening day with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown completing their first official practice with the franchise.

"With any team, we got to start somewhere, and then we got to get better and better, and just keep trying to reach our ceiling, right?" Nurse said. "That happens day-to-day. Can we get up tomorrow, like, 98% as excited as we did today? It's going to be hard to get as excited as we all were today, right?

"But we need to come back, and we need to keep climbing that mountain. That's a daily process. I just want them to reach their potential. If they do, great things are going to happen." -- Dave McMenamin
